positions.as_written: Read a patellofemoral contact study for how the quadriceps was loaded, because a single line of pull limits what the result describes.
Check the imaging protocol behind any threshold before applying it, since the same number means different things on different sequences and positions.
Read the pain literature as correlation and say so, rather than restating a correlation as a mechanism.
Read instability and pain separately even when a paper treats them together.
Weigh the patient's age and physiology, since skeletal maturity changes both the options and the natural history.
Weigh comorbidities, including the widespread pain and sensitisation that frequently accompany this presentation.
Weigh the demands on the knee, because deep flexion loading is where this joint declares itself.
Weigh their psychological state seriously here rather than as a formality, since anterior knee pain is the knee presentation where distress and symptom severity are most closely linked.
Read the instability literature for structural prediction and the pain literature for what it actually claims, which is less than it is usually quoted as claiming.
- Psychological state carries unusual weight in this presentation and should be weighed as evidence rather than as courtesy.
